clues: This city stands on a bend of a great river, the last good spot where boats from down south could land. A twin city faces it across the water.
Far north, with no large lakes near to soften the air, this place takes Arctic cold blasts head on. It is the coldest big city area in the whole land.
In 1849 a new territory was formed here, and this small river town was made its capital. It has kept that job ever since.
On a hill over the river bend stands the state capitol, a grand hall clad in bright marble. Lawmakers have met in its rooms since the year 1905.
The leaders of Minnesota make its laws in this city, in the capitol on the hill. The state chief and the top court work there too.
